source_refs.note: Use of Stem Cells: a main subheading of 3.8 Stem cells, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 88-88.

items: Regenerative Medicine: Stem cells have the potential to repair or replace damaged tissues and organs. Therefore, they are used for treating conditions such as spinal cord injuries, type 1 diabetes, Parkinson’s disease, and heart disease.

Drug Testing and Development: By differentiating stem cells into specific cell types, researchers can create models of human diseases, allowing for more accurate testing of drug effects and reducing the reliance on animal models.

Personalized Medicine: Stem cells can be derived from a patient’s own cells, reducing the risk of immune rejection when used in treatments. This personalized approach can lead to more effective and safer therapies.
